name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
hook: The Russian novelist of guilt, murder and salvation — Jeopardy's favorite existentialist.

facts.label: Crime and Punishment
facts.statement: Crime and Punishment (1866) follows Raskolnikov, a former student who murders a pawnbroker and her half-sister.

facts.label: Siberia
facts.statement: Raskolnikov confesses and gets eight years in Siberia; Dostoevsky himself had spent four years in a Siberian prison camp.

facts.label: Notes from Underground
facts.statement: Notes from Underground was called "the best overture to existentialism ever written" by Walter Kaufmann.

facts.label: The Brothers Karamazov
facts.statement: The Brothers Karamazov is his last novel; its brothers include a writer, a monastery student and one who did not work.

facts.label: The Gambler
facts.statement: Deep in debt, he wrote The Gambler in October 1866.

facts.label: St. Petersburg
facts.statement: Crime and Punishment unfolds in St. Petersburg, where his home is now a museum.

facts.label: The House of the Dead
facts.statement: Tolstoy considered The House of the Dead, from the 1860s, his countryman's masterpiece.
